title: Primary decomposition of a finite discrete representation
statement: Let G be a topological group, and M a discrete continuous integral representation [def-exc-discrete-modules-category] whose underlying abelian group is finite. There exist a natural number r, primes p_i for i in Fin r, and discrete continuous integral representations N_i with finite underlying groups, such that every element of the multiplicative version of N_i has p_i-power order. There are equivariant integral linear maps a_i from M to N_i and b_i from N_i to M for which the sum of a_i followed by b_i is the identity of M. The zero representation permits r = 0.

proof.text: Normalize the bundled Z-module structure using uniqueness of the integral module structure. Finiteness gives additive torsion, hence Module.IsTorsion Z M. Apply Mathlib Submodule.exists_isInternal_prime_power_torsion_of_pid to obtain a finite index type, irreducible integers p_i, exponents e_i and an internal direct sum of S_i = Submodule.torsionBy Z M (p_i ^ e_i). Use IsInternal.chooseDecomposition and decomposeLinearEquiv for its unique inverse.

Each S_i is invariant under the action because integral linear maps commute with scalar multiplication. Restrict the representation using Representation.subrepresentation. Equality in the subtype is equality in M, so each element has exactly its original open stabilizer. The subtype is finite. Int.prime_iff_natAbs_prime makes natAbs(p_i) prime, and smul_torsionBy together with natAbs_nsmul_eq_zero shows every element is killed by natAbs(p_i) ^ e_i; isPGroup_iff_pow_pow_eq_one gives the primary-group property.

Define P_i by composing the unique inverse of the internal direct-sum map with DirectSum.component. To prove P_i commutes with each action map, apply DirectSum.decompose_lhom_ext and check on S_j. On S_i the projection is identity; on every other S_j it is zero. The action preserves S_j, so both sides agree in either case. Construct a_i from P_i and b_i from the subtype inclusion as equivariant maps in the full subcategory.

DirectSum.sum_support_decompose says the sum of all nonzero components of x equals x. Enlarge its support to the whole finite index set: components outside the support are zero. Thus the sum over i of the inclusions of P_i(x) equals x, including the empty-index case.

Reindex the finite family along (Fintype.equivFin iota).symm. The full-subcategory inclusion functor is additive, so Functor.map_sum transfers the categorical sum to Rep. Rep.sum_hom and IntertwiningMap.sum_apply evaluate it pointwise. Fintype.sum_equiv and the preceding identity prove that the sum of a_i followed by b_i is the identity.

proof_origin.note: Mathlib PID internal primary decomposition replaces explicit exponent factorization and CRT coefficients; all representation and categorical glue is proved in Lean.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finite_primary_decomposition
    (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
    (M : DiscreteContinuousRep.{0, u, v} ℤ G) [Finite M.obj.V] :
    ∃ (r : ℕ) (p : Fin r → ℕ) (N : Fin r → DiscreteContinuousRep.{0, u, v} ℤ G),
      (∀ i, (p i).Prime) ∧ (∀ i, Finite (N i).obj.V) ∧
      (∀ i, IsPGroup (p i) (Multiplicative (N i).obj.V)) ∧
      ∃ (a : ∀ i, M ⟶ N i) (b : ∀ i, N i ⟶ M),
        ∑ i, a i ≫ b i = 𝟙 M
